correctness.rationale: All singular points lie on the heavy-coordinate line. Its generic stabilizer has order \(\gcd(a,b)\), so a positive-dimensional singular stratum occurs exactly when that gcd exceeds one; if the gcd is one, only the two endpoints can be singular. Writing \(d=b-a\), the canonical and terminal regions are respectively \(0\le d\le r,1\le a\le r+d\) and their strict versions. Since \(\gcd(a,b)=\gcd(a,d)\), counting coprime lattice points in those triangles gives \(1+\Phi(r)+(2\Phi(r)-1)=3\Phi(r)\) and the terminal formula with \(r-1\). Subtraction gives \(3\varphi(r)\), and the two boundary descriptions follow by the same gcd reduction. The actual verifier blob was inspected and an independent finite regression through \(r=100\) reproduced both census formulas.

originality.rationale: At the audited snapshot, a published result for the exact same family already gives the complete canonical and terminal parameter triangles \(0\le d\le r,1\le a\le r+d\) and the strict terminal version. Standard weighted-projective quotient geometry identifies the generic stabilizer on the heavy-coordinate line as \(\mu_{\gcd(a,b)}\), so zero-dimensional singular locus is exactly \(\gcd(a,b)=1\). The assigned formulas then reduce to the elementary count of coprime lattice points in the already-known triangle, using symmetry and the definition of the summatory totient. Under the required implication-level standard, this is a routine arithmetic corollary of stronger published structural data rather than an independent original theorem.
